analysis_steps.goal: Measure nuclear CO(5-4) flux, size and line width

method.value: uv-plane elliptical Gaussian fit with UV_FIT over 1680 km/s; spectrum from Gaussian with fixed parameters; Gaussian fit to spectrum

evidence.quote: We extracted the total CO(5-4) flux associated with UDF6462 through $uv$-plane fitting with an elliptical Gaussian model, using the GILDAS task UV_FIT.
The fitting was performed over a velocity range $\Delta$*v* $\simeq$ 1680 km s$^{-1}$

fitting.value: Free-parameter elliptical Gaussian with initial guesses at optical peak and beam

evidence.quote: As initial guesses for the model centre and size, we assumed the coordinates of the peak in the optical images and the ALMA synthesized beam, respectively, and let the parameters vary freely.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract clump spectra, stack and derive upper limits

method.value: Fit visibilities with multiple Gaussians at fixed clump positions/sizes on the residual uv-table after subtracting the nuclear model; velocity-shifted weighted mean stack; 3 sigma upper limits assuming 100 km/s FWHM

evidence.quote: the extraction was performed on the residual $uv$-table obtained after subtracting the best-fitting elliptical Gaussian model for the nuclear region described above.

findings_qualitative.value: CO(5-4) is more centrally concentrated than SFR tracers and dust, and this is not caused by observational bias

claims.hypothesis: Do UV-bright clumps show CO(5-4) emission?
claims.experiment: uv-plane extraction of clump spectra and stacking
claims.result: No detection; stack upper limit 9 mJy km/s
claims.finding: Clumps contribute <~18% of CO(5-4) emission, below their 10-40% SFR share

evidence.quote: None of the the six clumps in UDF6462 is instead detected at the depth of our CO(5-4) map.

claims.hypothesis: Clumps have high SFE or gas fractions above their host
claims.experiment: Convert stack limits to gas mass with simulation-motivated R51 and alpha_CO
claims.finding: Clumps not more gas-rich than host; SFE may be high, but dependent on SFR and conversion assumptions

evidence.quote: This is indicative of clump gas fractions that are not higher than that of their host galaxy and suggests that clumps may not be gas dominated.

claims.hypothesis: CO(5-4) distribution follows that of star formation and dust
claims.experiment: uv-plane size fit and simulated observations
claims.result: CO ~0.5 arcsec vs ~1 arcsec SFR and ~2 arcsec dust

evidence.loc: 5.1 Star formation, cold dust and CO(5$-$4) distribution
evidence.quote: We interpret the results of these tests as an indication that the CO(5-4) is truly more centrally concentrated than other star formation tracers or dust in UDF6462

claims.hypothesis: Nuclear region lies on the L_IR-L'CO(5-4) relation
claims.experiment: Compare nuclear L'CO and radio SFR with literature relations
claims.finding: Consistent with ongoing nuclear star formation

evidence.quote: The CO(5-4) measurement for the nuclear region places it on the correlations found in the existing literature.

why_this_method.value: CO(5-4) traces dense gas actually forming stars, a good tracer of clump star formation

evidence.quote: the CO(5-4) transition is particularly advantageous for studying star formation occurring in a dense, clumpy medium

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tau-model SFH maps rejected for clump properties due to noise and step-like SFH variations

evidence.quote: this map is not considered further for deriving clump properties

limitations_admitted.value: Clump SFRs vary by up to ~1 dex between methods and clump R51/alpha_CO are poorly constrained

evidence.quote: the SFR estimates for individual clumps can vary by up to $\sim$1 dex

referee_caveats_inferred: Clump gas mass limits depend on assumed R51, alpha_CO and line width
